profiles.meeting_scenario: A weekly coordination meeting between the modeling and platform workstreams for an ML research paper and internal demo on cost-effective deployment of distilled BERT models in a serverless environment. The team has already distilled and fine-tuned compact models for sentiment analysis and semantic textual similarity, and now needs to align on the handoff from model artifacts to deployment benchmarking so the final evaluation section can be completed. The agenda is to confirm which model package will be handed over, what counts as the 'production-like' serverless benchmark setup, how results will be reported across the two tasks, and where the shared evaluation bundle will live. The expected outcome is that both members leave believing they have aligned on the deployment package, benchmark procedure, reporting format, and ownership of the shared artifacts needed for next week's results review.

members.name: Dr. Nina Park
members.expertise: knowledge distillation, transformer fine-tuning, offline evaluation for NLP tasks
members.background: Nina leads the modeling side of an industry research project and recently produced distilled BERT checkpoints for domain-specific sentiment analysis and semantic textual similarity using internal datasets and a standard offline evaluation pipeline.
members.private_state: She wants the deployment benchmark to reflect the exact model variant and preprocessing stack used in her latest experiments so the paper narrative stays clean, and she is worried that platform-side packaging changes could invalidate comparability with her offline results.
hidden_assumptions: When people refer to the 'final model', they mean the best-performing checkpoint selected after her last full validation sweep, even if the serialization format changes later.
The 'eval bundle' naturally includes tokenizer files, label maps, threshold settings, and the lightweight preprocessing notebook she used to generate canonical inputs.

A 'production-like benchmark' should preserve research-time request semantics, including warm runs after initialization is complete, because that is what makes latency numbers comparable across model variants.
Reporting 'the results' for the deployment section means one aggregate line per task using the same summary numbers already used in her draft tables.

members.name: Arjun Mehta
members.expertise: serverless inference, model packaging, latency/cost benchmarking, CI deployment workflows
members.background: Arjun owns the deployment and benchmarking workstream for the project and has been converting transformer models into serverless-friendly artifacts, setting up Lambda-style functions, and measuring latency and cost under production-shaped invocation patterns.
members.private_state: He wants to keep the deployment pipeline simple and reproducible in CI, and he is concerned that any artifact depending on ad hoc research-side preprocessing or notebook outputs will slow down the benchmark schedule.
hidden_assumptions: When people say the 'final model', they mean the deployable packaged artifact that has passed size and startup constraints in the serverless runtime, even if it was converted from a slightly earlier checkpoint.

The 'eval bundle' means a compact tarball with model weights, tokenizer vocab, and a small JSON schema for requests; thresholds and analysis notebooks are not part of a deployment handoff unless explicitly requested.
A 'production-like benchmark' includes cold starts and default autoscaling behavior because those are unavoidable in real serverless use and matter for cost claims.
Reporting 'the results' for the deployment section means task-level latency/cost breakdowns by memory tier and invocation mode, with accuracy only as a compatibility check.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They both refer to handing off and benchmarking the 'final model'.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the best validation-performing distilled checkpoint from her latest run, with the exact preprocessing assumptions used in the research pipeline.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the deployable serverless artifact that fits package and startup constraints, potentially exported from an earlier or slightly modified checkpoint after optimization.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both assume 'final model' is an obvious phrase because each workstream usually has a single canonical endpoint artifact, so the term sounds fully aligned and does not trigger clarification.

misalignment_points.topic: What is included in the 'eval bundle'
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree that Nina will drop the 'eval bundle' into the shared workspace for Arjun to use.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 thinks this bundle includes everything needed to reproduce task outputs exactly: model card notes, tokenizer, label map, task-specific thresholds, canonical request examples, and the preprocessing notebook-derived input formatting conventions.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 thinks the bundle is only the minimal deployment handoff package: model artifact, tokenizer vocab, and request/response schema, excluding notebook assets and task-specific decision thresholds.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In both research and systems teams, 'bundle' usually refers to a packaged set of files, and because each believes their own default contents are standard, neither thinks to enumerate the boundaries.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to run the benchmark in a 'production-like' serverless setup before the next review.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 thinks 'production-like' means realistic request payloads and the same model behavior as production, but latency should be measured after initialization so model-to-model comparisons are stable and not dominated by cold-start variance.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 thinks 'production-like' means including cold starts, default memory tiers under consideration, and bursty invocation patterns because those determine real operational cost and user-visible latency in serverless systems.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both endorse realism and production relevance, but they silently optimize for different comparability standards; the phrase sounds shared precisely because both see their interpretation as the normal meaning.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They discuss updating 'the results table' for next week's review.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is thinking of the paper draft table that has one summary row per task, where deployment numbers will be inserted alongside accuracy metrics.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is thinking of the internal benchmarking spreadsheet with separate rows by memory allocation, cold/warm mode, and request batch profile.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: There are multiple well-known result artifacts in the project, but both are habitually referred to as 'the results table' within their own subteams, so the phrase feels singular and mutually understood.
